h1:
Nakhon Pathom & Kanchanaburi, 2 Days 1 Night
Temples Then Nature
intro: Nakhon Pathom and Kanchanaburi sit right next to each other, only about 65 kilometres apart, so it's easy to roll both provinces into a single trip. Spend the first day temple-hopping and eating well in Nakhon Pathom, then cross into Kanchanaburi on day two for Erawan Falls and a ride on the Death Railway. Here's a 2-day, 1-night plan paced so you're never rushing, with real distances and a real budget.

blocks.html: This trip suits anyone who wants both merit-making and nature in one go. Driving yourself is easiest since the stops are spread out, but if you don't have a car there are vans and trains to connect the dots. The main decision is whether to sleep in Nakhon Pathom and do Kanchanaburi as a day trip, or move over and stay riverside in Kanchanaburi instead. We went with the latter so we could be at the falls early, before the crowds.

items: Bangkok → Nakhon Pathom — about 60 km, 1–1.5 hr depending on traffic
Nakhon Pathom → Kanchanaburi (town) — about 65 km, around 1 hr; the open sections of the M81 motorway cut the time down
Kanchanaburi town → Erawan Falls — about 65 km, 1–1.5 hr into Si Sawat district
Overnight — 1 night by the River Kwai in Kanchanaburi town, roughly halfway

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Erawan Falls is inside a national park, so there's an entry fee, and weekend mornings get very busy. If you want it quiet and open, aim to be at the gate before 9am, and check whether it's a high-water or low-water period. The rainy season has fuller, prettier water but the paths get slippery.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Nakhon Pathom trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Temples, good food, sleep in Kanchanaburi

items.note: A stupa 120.5 metres tall, the tallest in Thailand. Walk a loop around it, pray and make a wish. There are souvenir stalls and breakfast snacks around the base. Come early while the sun is still soft.
The palace of King Rama VI, just a few minutes from Phra Pathom Chedi. The exhibition buildings are open 09:00–16:00, while the surrounding gardens are open for strolling and photos until evening.

items.activity: Wat Rai Khing, Sam Phran district
items.note: Pay respects to Luang Pho Wat Rai Khing, a temple on the Tha Chin River, open 08:00–16:00. In front of the temple there's a market and riverside restaurants.

items.activity: Lunch at Don Wai Floating Market
items.note: An old market on the Tha Chin River. The local stars are five-spice braised duck, boat noodles and old-style Thai sweets. You can take a short boat ride for the views too.
About 1 hr into Kanchanaburi town. Check in to a place by the River Kwai and rest up before the evening.
The walking street and riverside spots in Kanchanaburi town. Have dinner with the sunset and save your energy for the next day.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Erawan Falls and the Death Railway

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Swim at the falls, ride the cliffside railway

items.note: Drive 1–1.5 hr into Si Sawat district. Have a light breakfast before you go, or grab something to eat at a rest stop along the way.

A seven-tier waterfall; the walk from the bottom tier to the very top is about 1.5 km. Tiers 2 and 3 have emerald-green pools you can swim in, while the upper tiers get steeper. Bring non-slip shoes and drinking water.

items.activity: Lunch and a change of clothes
items.note: There are restaurants to pick from in front of the park. Let yourself dry off before moving on.
A historic World War II bridge you can walk across, close to town. Around it are museums and souvenir shops.

items.activity: Ride the Death Railway, Tham Krasae section
items.note: The prettiest stretch, where the track hugs the cliff along the Khwae Noi River. Check the train times ahead since there are only a few runs a day. The curve along the wooden trestle bridge is the highlight.
If you still have the energy and the time, you can stop at the Hellfire Pass Memorial, but check the hours first as it closes at 4pm and has an annual maintenance closure mid-year.

blocks.title: About Hellfire Pass
blocks.html: The Hellfire Pass Memorial is free to enter, open 09:00–16:00, with a walking trail along the old railway cutting. In 2026 there's an annual maintenance closure from 4–24 May, so if you plan to stop, check the date first. And if day two is running tight, it's fine to skip it and save it for next time.

items: Fuel/transport — about ฿1,000–1,500 round trip from Bangkok if you drive, depending on the car
1 night riverside — from about ฿800–2,500 per night depending on the standard and the view
Erawan Falls entry — there's a park fee for people and the car, so allow a few hundred per group
Death Railway — tickets run from tens to a few hundred baht per person depending on the stretch and seat class
Food — about ฿150–400 per person per meal, including souvenirs from Nakhon Pathom and Kanchanaburi
Rough total — a 2-day, 1-night trip for 2 people comes to about ฿3,500–6,000 depending on your style

blocks.text: Can you do it without your own car?

blocks.html: You can, but you'll need to plan around the schedules more. From Bangkok there are vans and trains to Nakhon Pathom and on to Kanchanaburi. Within Kanchanaburi town there are songthaews and motorbike taxis. Erawan Falls is far from town, though, so people without a car usually book a half-day tour or hire a car with a driver for the day. It works out cheaper and you won't be sweating the timing of the last ride back.

items.name: Sleep in Nakhon Pathom, day-trip Kanchanaburi
items.blurb: Good if you're on a budget. You catch only the Kanchanaburi highlights in a single day, but it's more tiring and more rushed.

items.name: Move over and stay riverside in Kanchanaburi
items.blurb: The plan we recommend. Wake up early to swim before the crowds, and the riverside setting makes the overnight worth it.

faq.q: How far apart are Nakhon Pathom and Kanchanaburi, and how long is the drive?
faq.a: Nakhon Pathom town to Kanchanaburi town is about 65 kilometres, around 1 hour by car. Using the open sections of the M81 motorway trims that further. From Kanchanaburi town on to Erawan Falls is another 1–1.5 hours of driving.

faq.q: Can this trip be done in a single day?
faq.a: You can if you cut some stops, for example sticking to just Phra Pathom Chedi in Nakhon Pathom and then heading straight to the Bridge over the River Kwai and the train. But you won't make it to Erawan Falls, which is far out. If you want the falls too, stay one night in Kanchanaburi.

Erawan Falls is fullest and most colourful from late rainy season into early cool season (roughly September–December). In hot season the water can drop. That said, long holiday weekends are packed in every season, so aim to reach the falls before 9am.

faq.q: Is Hellfire Pass Memorial always open?
faq.a: It's free to enter every day, 09:00–16:00, but in 2026 there's an annual maintenance closure from 4–24 May, so check your travel date first if you plan to stop. Also keep a little aside for the deposit on the audio-guide equipment.

faq.q: Can young children and older travellers manage it?
faq.a: Phra Pathom Chedi, Wat Rai Khing, the Bridge over the River Kwai and Don Wai Floating Market are all easy walking and suit every age. The lower tiers of Erawan Falls are easy too, but tiers 4–7 get steep and slippery. Older travellers can stick to tiers 1–3 and still get the beauty.
